summary: Verified bug fix: Super Admin can now access /quotations and all other menus without 403. Frontend hasPerm role-based bypass for super_admin works. Regression RBAC still enforced for Sales (no Generate Invoice/Record Payment on booking detail) and Accounting (no New Quotation button on /quotations, Forbidden on /sales).
critical_code_review_comments: hasPerm super_admin bypass is a good defensive fix; consider also refreshing /auth/me on route change or after backend role/permission mutations so cached permissions don't go stale for non-super-admin roles either.
test_credentials: Super Admin: dedyirawan18@gmail.com/Admin@123; Sales: sales@safarcrm.com/Sales@123; Accounting: accounting@safarcrm.com/Account@123
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fixed and verified. AuthContext.hasPerm returns true for user.role==='super_admin'. All 8 Super Admin routes load without Forbidden. Sales booking detail correctly hides invoice.manage/payment.manage actions. Accounting correctly lacks New Quotation button on /quotations and gets Forbidden on /sales. 403 console errors while Accounting loads /quotations are expected (GET /api/quotations denied by backend since role lacks quotation.view — but ROUTE_PERMS lets them view the page shell; consider tightening to block route too, but not part of this bug).
rca of the issue: Root cause: Frontend RequirePermission guard relied purely on cached permissions from /auth/me. After Phase 4 introduced new permissions like quotation.view, super_admin sessions with stale /me responses did not include the new perm, causing the guard to render Forbidden. Fix: hasPerm now short-circuits to true when user.role==='super_admin', mirroring backend which grants ALL_PERMISSIONS to super_admin. Verified by direct navigation to /quotations and all other menus.
